newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia bonds hold their ground vs dlr bloc.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia bonds hold their ground vs dlr bloc.

text.p: Australian bonds held their ground against other dollar bloc bonds during a slow trading session and yields spreads tightened.

The most notable move was against New Zealand debt which came under pressure after comments by RBNZ governor Don Brash, who called for fiscal restraint to curb the N.Z. dollar following last month's inconclusive election.
He also said that it seemed to have become popular wisdom that investing in N.Z. dollar assets was a "virtually riskless exercise," and a more realistic understanding of the situation was needed.
New Zealand's 10-year bond yield spread went back to a premium over Australia for the first time since mid-October.

The local market also outperformed Canadian bonds, particularly the short-end, after last Friday's 25 basis point easing by the Bank of Canada. The BOC is seen holding policy for now, which has encouraged switching to the long end of the Canadian curve.
Meanwhile, U.S. Treasuries face a key inflation data week after today's holiday for Veteran's Day with PPI and CPI due out on Wednesday and Thursday respectively.
The Federal Open Market Committee also meets on Wednesday, although no policy change is expected.
